safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any noted behavior, condition, or situation in the workplace that relates to health and safety, whether positive or negative. In HSE analytics, these are proactive reports made by workers or supervisors to identify safe practices or potential risks before they result in incidents. Safety observations help organizations monitor compliance, identify trends, and improve safety culture.
examples: Observed worker wearing proper PPE in the welding area.
Noticed blocked emergency exit during routine inspection.
Reported that all fire extinguishers were in place and accessible.
Saw a forklift operator using seatbelt as required.
Identified a spill in the loading dock and notified cleaning crew.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near miss reports are critical for identifying hazards and preventing future incidents by addressing underlying causes before harm occurs. These are often used to improve safety processes and raise awareness.
examples: A falling tool narrowly missed a worker passing below.
Forklift reversed into a walkway but stopped before hitting anyone.
Chemical container slipped but was caught before spilling.
Worker tripped over a hose but regained balance without falling.
Overhead load swung out of control but did not strike equipment.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to determine root causes and prevent recurrence. Incidents can range from minor injuries to major accidents.
examples: Worker suffered a laceration while handling sharp metal.
Forklift collided with storage rack causing minor damage.
Oil spill occurred during equipment maintenance.
Employee slipped on wet floor and sprained ankle.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short circuit.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a potential source of harm or unsafe condition in the workplace. In HSE, these reports are used to proactively address risks before they lead to incidents or injuries. Hazard reports are essential for risk assessment and corrective action planning.
examples: Reported exposed wiring near the main entrance.
Identified unguarded machinery in the production area.
Noticed chemical drums stored without proper labeling.
Flagged loose handrails on the stairwell.
Observed oil leak under hydraulic press.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any condition, event, or behavior that may impact the environment, such as pollution, waste, or resource use. In HSE, these observations help monitor compliance with environmental regulations and identify opportunities for improvement in environmental performance.
examples: Observed oil sheen on surface water near the facility.
Noticed improper disposal of chemical containers.
Reported excessive dust emissions from the crusher.
Identified leaking waste bins in the storage yard.
Saw wildlife entering restricted waste area.

quality_issue.name: quality_issue
quality_issue.description: A quality issue refers to any deviation from established standards or specifications that could affect product integrity, safety, or compliance. In HSE, quality issues are reported to prevent defective products, rework, or safety risks arising from non-conforming materials or processes.
examples: Found welds not meeting inspection criteria on pressure vessel.
Reported batch of paint with incorrect color mix.
Identified missing safety labels on finished products.
Detected cracks in castings during quality check.
Observed packaging not sealed properly.

maintenance_request.name: maintenance_request
maintenance_request.description: A maintenance request is a formal notification to repair, replace, or service equipment, infrastructure, or safety systems. In HSE, timely maintenance requests help prevent equipment failures, unsafe conditions, and ensure compliance with safety standards.
examples: Requested repair of faulty emergency lighting in corridor.
Submitted work order for leaking air compressor.
Reported malfunctioning fire alarm panel.
Requested replacement of worn-out safety harnesses.
Notified maintenance about broken guard on conveyor.

injury_report.name: injury_report
injury_report.description: An injury report documents any work-related harm or physical injury sustained by an employee, regardless of severity. In HSE, these reports are essential for legal compliance, medical follow-up, and root cause analysis to prevent recurrence.
examples: Worker reported a cut finger from handling sheet metal.
Employee suffered a back strain while lifting heavy box.
Technician burned hand during hot work operation.
Operator twisted ankle stepping off uneven platform.
Contractor received eye irritation from chemical splash.

property_damage.name: property_damage
property_damage.description: Property damage refers to any harm, breakage, or loss affecting company assets, equipment, or infrastructure. In HSE, property damage reports help track incidents that may impact operations, safety, or require repairs and insurance claims.
examples: Forklift struck and damaged warehouse racking.
Storm caused roof panels to detach from building.
Spilled solvent corroded floor surface.
Vehicle collision resulted in dented loading dock door.
Broken window reported in control room.

unsafe_condition.name: unsafe_condition
unsafe_condition.description: An unsafe condition is any physical state or environmental factor in the workplace that could lead to injury, illness, or property damage if not corrected. In HSE, reporting unsafe conditions is crucial for hazard control and accident prevention.
examples: Wet floor without warning signs in main hallway.
Guardrail missing on elevated platform.
Poor lighting in emergency exit route.
Obstructed fire extinguisher access.
Unstable stack of pallets in storage area.

unsafe_act.name: unsafe_act
unsafe_act.description: An unsafe act is any behavior or action by a person that increases the risk of injury, illness
